title: BADBOX 3.0: malware preinstalled on off-brand TV boxes drives ad fraud and residential proxy networks
date_note: Publication date of the GBHackers article; the HUMAN Satori report page states no date.
place: United States (traffic cited; devices span many countries)
geo_basis: country; the report cites US traffic, victims are worldwide
actor: BADBOX operators (Satori links the module catalog to Chinese manufacturer TXCZ)
summary: HUMAN's Satori team reports BADBOX 3.0, a backdoor in off-brand Android TV boxes that loads modules for hidden video-ad fraud and for residential proxy exits. At peak it generated roughly 40 billion bid requests a day, more than 4% of connected-TV traffic HUMAN observes. Satori links the module catalog to TXCZ; it calls this linkage, not formal attribution.
plain: Cheap TV boxes sold without Google certification can arrive already infected. They secretly play ads and let strangers route traffic through the owner's home internet.
exec: Infected consumer devices feed ad fraud and proxy networks used for account takeover and carding traffic that looks like it comes from homes.
action: Buy only Google Play Protect certified streaming devices from known brands; retire or isolate off-brand boxes that behave oddly or generate unexplained traffic.
impact: Peak of roughly 40 billion bid requests per day; devices enrolled in 11 residential proxy networks; no infection count given for BADBOX 3.0.
products: Android Open Source Project TV boxes (off-brand)

validation.note: Primary report by HUMAN Satori read (partly via extraction, page truncated); GBHackers article read and consistent on the figures.

review.note: Read HUMAN Satori and GBHackers: 40B bid requests/day at peak, over 4% CTV, 11 proxy networks, TXCZ linked not attributed, no BADBOX 3.0 infection count; date_note matches
